decisions.summary: TempDir::new runs sweep_dead inside a std::sync::Once: the process's first TempDir lists the temp directory, no later one does.
decisions.why: Performance work the GM asked to come first (2026-11-20, 'can we in general priotitize performance improvements going forward?'). It is T365's lever A as measured. It removes repeated listings and keeps the removal rule: dead pid, three-hour age, directory test.

decisions.summary: sweep_dead takes no tag and reads the name from its end (l7r-, anything, -p<pid>, -<seq>), so one listing takes every tag's leftovers, hyphenated tags included (the 29 l7r-gate-ci-stop-handler leftovers).
decisions.why: This stays within what was asked. The section says it removes the same set of names as before, taken over all tags, and sooner. The guards that protect work are unchanged: dead pid, three-hour age, directory test. It serves the GM's disk words (2026-11-22: 'clean up after ourselves in terms of the file system'; 2026-11-25: 'this container specifically is leaving artifacts sitting around'). No GM words in the bundle protect a dead process's l7r-<x>-p<pid>-<seq> directory older than three hours. So the wider reach (leftovers of tags this process never makes) is not a narrowing and needs no ruling. The search-space gap in the '.keep()' grep is reported apart from this verdict, as a finding for the builder; it does not block.

decisions.summary: Kept and pinned in a_gone_process_s_directories_go_with_the_next_process_of_any_tag: the pre-T101 form, hook-suite directories, l7r-test-scratch, files, a live pid's, anything changed within three hours, untagged names and names not opening l7r-.
decisions.why: This keeps the constraints the section reports from the GM's 2026-11-11 words as tempdir.rs quotes them: a leftover younger than three hours, and the form before T101, are not touched. Those words are not in this bundle, so this ruling rests on the section's report of them. It also keeps T365's rule that nothing a later run could reuse is deleted.

decisions.summary: A leftover now goes at the next process's first TempDir of any tag, which is sooner. A process that changes its TMPDIR after its first TempDir does not sweep the second directory.
decisions.why: Cleanup comes sooner in the common case. In the TMPDIR edge the leftover is still removed by a later process whose first TempDir is there, so nothing is lost. A difference from the old behavior is not a defect (constitution XIV), and no caller is said to do this.

decisions.summary: Of the task line's two routes, the plan takes the cleanup once a run: hookrun.sh --sweep on the Makefile's fan-out line before xargs. It does not move the suites' directories under one subdirectory.
decisions.why: The section says the task line offers two routes; the task line itself is not in the bundle. Either route is performance work the GM asked to come first (2026-11-20), and the GM gave no instruction on which to take. The route chosen moves no path, and the grep the section cites (with its method) shows three places that know the path's shape.

decisions.summary: The cleanup loop becomes the function sweep_gone, with unchanged removal. --sweep runs it and exits; --swept skips it; a job without the mark sweeps as before. The mark is a command word, not an exported variable, so nested runners in test-parts.2/3 still sweep.
decisions.why: This is a mechanism for doing the cleanup once a run. What it removes is unchanged, and a job run by hand or by a test keeps its old behavior.

decisions.summary: A suite run alone stays untouched, and a suite's TMPDIR stays <temp>/l7r-hooks-suite-<guard>-p<pid>.<x>.

decisions.summary: A killed runner's leftover now waits for the next make hooks-test run that has a suite to run, where before it waited for the next suite of any run.

decisions.id: T346: holder read at the run's start
decisions.summary: tiers::carries books a carry to the last pool-log take of the tree at or before the carry run's START, not its end
decisions.why: Fixes a wrong outcome in the task time breakdown the GM asked for (2026-11-25, T243): the 2026-11-26 carry of T301's work was booked to T308. Naming the right task is what the breakdown is for.

decisions.id: T346: a tree nobody held at the start is no task's carry
decisions.summary: an unheld tree at run start books to no task, as a tree with no take already did
decisions.why: Keeps the existing rule for an unheld tree. The section's 27-carry pass over the pinned window found one carry re-booked and none lost, so nothing the breakdown counted is dropped.

decisions.id: T346: the carry's time stays its run's end
decisions.summary: only the holder changes; batches still compares the run's end with the landing's
decisions.why: Changes nothing the task line asks to change.

decisions.summary: make task-progress reads the same function, so its staged list and carried lines name the start holder
decisions.why: Serves the GM's live view (2026-11-26, T293). The section measured a one-line diff in the old and new outputs, the expected one.

decisions.id: T382: own lines outside every span open a span
decisions.summary: an agent's own line outside its spans opens a span to its next stop, else to span_end's end
decisions.why: Fixes a wrong outcome: 557.5 builder-minutes over 2026-11-21 to 11-24 were left out of the builder column while their turns were booked. The GM asked for everything measured (2026-11-22) and every minute named (amendment (c)). The section measured that no new span crosses a stopped stretch.

decisions.id: T382: span starts at the first own line, not the stop
decisions.summary: the stop to the next own line stays T345's 'builders: stopped' time
decisions.why: Avoids counting the same minutes twice, which would itself distort the breakdown.

decisions.summary: a single own line with no later line or stop opens no span; an agent with no start line takes its kind from its first stop that names one, else ?
decisions.why: A lone line has no duration to book. Taking the kind from a stop keeps review agents out of the builder column, as the GM's split of reviewing from code work asks (2026-11-25). This is detail inside the requested fix and narrows nothing.

decisions.id: T382: new spans are in flight for waits
decisions.summary: Flight::book treats a new span like a started one, so blocking rises 3539.9 to 3550.8 in the 2026-11-22 window
decisions.why: Under the GM's definition (l), a wait booked to a builder that was working is a wait on that builder. A session waiting on a builder inside a span that the lines show it working is blocking on that work.

decisions.id: T346, T382: two pinned tests restated
decisions.summary: a_resumed_builder_is_booked_in_every_span_and_stopped_between_them and the_columns_book_make_runs_compile_and_until restated to the new readings
decisions.why: The tests pinned the wrong readings. Under fix-as-we-go (GM 2026-11-18), checks change as the defect they pinned is fixed. New red-first tests carry each rule.

decisions.summary: counted as performance work for scheduling
decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-20: 'this kind of measurement task to be counted as a performance task for the purpose of scheduling and coming first'.

decisions.id: T346 (found and left): a bundle's carry is no task's, filed as T393
decisions.summary: tiers::batches splits a bundle's pool detail '451 T324,T345' on whitespace only, so a bundle's carry is booked to no task; not fixed here, filed T393, lands before T380
decisions.why: This is a real defect left. It is a different one from either task line: how a bundle's pool detail is parsed, not when the holder is read. Fixing it needs a new rule for which bundled task a carry run books to. The GM's own words cover filing it: 2026-11-22, 'not bother cutting back on new tasks filed ... we can file new tasks just as fast as we are now if we bundle them together when fixing them'. It is filed and ordered, not dropped. The purpose test holds: T346's own measured mis-booking (T301/T308) and every other non-bundle carry are fixed by this section, so the deferral does not gut what T346 asked. T332 and T344 are pre-existing open tasks the section reports, not decisions it makes.

decisions.summary: T383: the reversal read moves whole to a new event_log_hooks/reversal.rs because event_log_hooks.rs stood at the 1,000-line file-scale bar
decisions.why: A file layout choice made to keep the file-scale rule; nothing asked for is narrowed and no behavior changes.

decisions.summary: T383: a path with more than one JSON spelling (quote, backslash, control, DEL, non-ASCII, non-string) is screened by the Edit tool name alone, and its lines are parsed as before
decisions.why: A strict superset of the old read's lines followed by the old parse test word for word, so the tripwire keeps every catch. It is safer than the task line's sketch, and that sketch is the coordinating session's, not the GM's (the request holds no words on the tripwire or the session name, grep of request.md). Serves FR-013, performance first.

decisions.summary: T383: a printable-ASCII path with no quote or backslash is screened by its own JSON text, trusting that no writer escapes a printable ASCII character it need not
decisions.why: This is the one place a put-back could be missed. The stated trust is checked against the real writers (serde and events-refile; every line of 34 logs in serde compact form), and the differential over 468,589 real lines dropped 0 of the 8,661 lines the old read used, with 0 of 1,806 paths differing. No wrong outcome is shown anywhere, so the constraint that no reversal is missed holds.

decisions.summary: T383: the side file of Edit lines, the second option on the task line, is not built; the screen is chosen and the remaining whole-log read is filed
decisions.why: The task line names two options and the plan picks one, with a stated reason (no second file to drift, no missed reversal). The request asks for performance work first, not for a particular mechanism, so nothing asked for is dropped.

decisions.summary: T385: the transcript is read backward in 64 KiB blocks (BLOCK, a GUESS knob) and stops at the last custom-title record; what one line says is the old loop body unchanged
decisions.why: The same last-rename-wins name comes out at every block size; a test checks this against the forward read kept as its oracle. A performance change inside FR-013.

decisions.summary: T385: a custom-title line that parses but is no object, standing before the last good record, no longer ends the lookup with no name; the good record names the session
decisions.why: A different output, said openly and pinned by a test, not a wrong outcome: the session gets its last real rename where before it got no name. Under the no-exactness rule (constitution XIII, the GM 2026-11-18) such a difference is the rule, not an exception, and needs no ruling.

decisions.summary: T385: a transcript that opens and then fails mid-read gives no name, as one that cannot be opened always did, instead of the name read before the failure
decisions.why: A different output with a stated reason (a name from part of a file can be the wrong name; the Python original raised), and a test pins it. No wrong outcome is shown; routing and the guard log already handle no name, the outcome for a file that cannot be opened.

decisions.summary: The Edit hook still reads the whole feature log, 78 ms of a worktree's 90 ms after this task; this is filed as T392, to land before T302
decisions.why: A remaining wait is not a wrong outcome under the defect definition (constitution XIV v2.36.0), so no defect is carried forward. It is filed with its reason, its task id and its order anyway, and as performance work it keeps its priority under FR-013.

decisions.summary: clone_sync_hooks pretool asks cx.session.canonical() only inside the misrouted(...) argument, after the dirty-clone return; no new branch, every verdict and message unchanged
decisions.why: A performance task (FR-013; the GM 2026-11-20 'prioritize performance improvements'): the name is read only on the path that judges by it, so the dirty-clone Edit stops reading the transcript; the clean path is untouched and the block keeps every verdict (constitution XIII).

decisions.summary: red-first test a_dirty_clones_edit_reads_no_transcript counts Session::reads (1 before, 0 after) and pins the clean path still reading
decisions.why: Enforcement of the change the task makes and of the unchanged clean path; it only fails when the requested speed-up is absent or the clean verdict path stops reading the name. Not unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: T373's lever F (git diff-index --quiet HEAD before git status --porcelain) declined, and its cure (update-index --refresh first) not taken
decisions.why: Lever F is the session's own proposal, not the GM's words; the block measures that it gives wrong verdicts (a stat-touched clean clone judged dirty skips misrouted's refusals and behind's fast-forward; an untracked file still owes the status call, slowing the clean path) - a defect it would introduce - and the cure would reintroduce an index write under its lock that 451 T304 removed. Declining a lever that changes verdicts narrows nothing the GM asked; prioritizing performance does not ask for a speed-up that breaks a guard.

decisions.why: Sequencing only; the remaining clean/untitled cost is named to T386 rather than left unowned, so no known defect is carried and nothing is narrowed.

decisions.why: No wrong outcome is involved: every verdict is kept, so constitution XIV's defect rules do not reach it; the slower clean-untitled row is the unchanged path under load, as the block states, not a regression the code could cause (it does strictly less on the dirty path and the same on the clean one).
